problem: A genuine tax correction rebuilds the complete allocation batch at its actual current time; first historical closing currently excludes those replacement shares solely because their effective_at is after the period cutoff, although their underlying business costs belong to the period.

policy.firstHistoricalClosing: Recognize a traceable late-produced allocation by the real business attribution of its complete source costs, not solely by the allocation generation timestamp.
policy.qualification: Verify the complete actual source set, allocation lineage, source versions, amounts, classifications and applicable correction evidence under the existing producer and atomic-command boundaries.

scope: First-period prepare/source rows, locked qualification and final capture use one consistent late-allocation qualification policy.
Retain genuine producer timestamps, full in-period source membership, immutable allocation/correction evidence and deterministic complete-batch amounts.
Keep realtime semantics, frozen-period restatement lineage, historical budget selection272 and current G/H authority boundaries intact.
Update the period270/271 acceptance adapters and public readiness presentation only where the actual changed behavior requires it; no route or persistence expansion.
minimumAcceptance: Real post-period tax correction followed by first historical closing includes the complete eligible in-period allocation share.
A batch containing a genuine post-period source cost cannot enter the old period by trimming or relabeling its members.
Missing or changed source, allocation or correction evidence is rejected without partial necessary writes.
Nohead/head first closing and existing-period restatement preserve the frozen budget and realtime current authority rules.
Independent code review precedes exact combined build, admission and genuine end-to-end acceptance.
